To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Gross-Neueu model near the transition temperature exhibits a critical evolution, which is characterized by a nontrivial, nonlocal structure of the classical solutions, and by the formation of a critical surface in rapidity, which separates the quark-guon and the hadronic phases.

the critical evolution of the system formed in relativistic heavy-ion collisions is described by the Gross-Neueu model, that the Ginzburg Landau approximation of the theory is applicable near the critical temperature, and that the solutions of the model reveal some interesting and measurable inhomogenieties.

the Gross-Neueu model at finite temperature, with appropriate boundary conditions imposed on the solutions, can be used to describe the longitudinal, critical behavior of the quark-hadronic system, formed in ion collisions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the critical behavior of the quark-hadronic phase transition in relativistically ion collisions.
the study of the Gross- Neveu model at finite temperature.

the study of the quark-hadronic phase transition in relativisic ion collisions, and with the search for a mechanism, that can lead to the formation of the hadronic matter in a form of a critical droplet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Gross-Neueu model, at finite temperature, provides a very useful framework for the description of the longitudinal evolution of the quarks and gluons, formed in relativisitic ion collisions.
the Gross-Neueu model at finite temperature is a good model for the quark-hadronic phase transition.
the quark-guon plasma phase transition in the early stages of the relativistic ion collisions can be reliably studied, in the framework of the 2D Gross-NeveU model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Gross-Neueu model, with the boundary conditions imposed by causality, predicts the formation of a shock wave in the rapidity distribution of hadrons, produced in relativistic ion collision, at the critical temperature.
the Gross-Neueu model at finite temperature, in the Ginzburg–Landau regime, is an ideal laboratory for the study of the quark-hadronic phase transition.

the Gross-Neueu model at finite temperature, when studied in the Ginzburg- Landau approximation, provides a mechanism for quark- hadron phase transition in the relativistic ion collisions which can be tested in the forthcoming experiments at the Brookhaven AGS and the CERN-SPS.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the critical evolution of the QCD plasma can be described in terms of classical solutions of a simple field theory model, and that the resulting rapidity distributions are sensitive to the details of the boundary conditions.

the critical evolution of the QGP, formed in relativisitic ion collisions, is not a smooth process, as is commonly assumed, but rather is characterized by the formation of a sharp interface between the QGP and the hadronic phase.
, at least in principle, the critical behavior in the quark-hadronic system, formed in ion collisions, can indeed be observed and studied experimentally.
